info.title: Queue OpenAPI for veed/dubbing
info.description: VEED Dubbing Standard translates spoken video into 86 languages with cloned voices and synchronized lip movements, preserving each speaker’s tone and emotion. It accepts videos up to 10 minutes long, detects the source language automatically or uses an explicit language setting, and supports keyterms for names, brands, and other terminology. Regional language tags resolve to their base language.

target_language.description: Language to dub into. This model has no regional dialects: a regional tag such as 'fr-FR' is accepted and dubbed in the base language ('fr').
target_language.title: Target Language

keyterms.description: Names and terms to get right in the dub, such as brand, product or people's names: they help the speech recognition catch these words and the translation keep them as written. Up to 1,000 terms, each at most 50 characters and 5 words, without the characters < > { } [ ] \.
keyterms.title: Keyterms

video_url.description: Video to dub, 8 seconds to 10 minutes long and with speech in its audio track. The speech is translated into the target language, and the speakers' lips are synced to the dubbed voices.
video_url.title: Video Url

source_language.description: Language spoken in the video. 'auto' (the default) detects it; set it explicitly if detection picks the wrong language.
source_language.title: Source Language

video.description: The dubbed video, with the speakers' lips synced to the translated speech

content_type.description: The mime type of the file.
content_type.title: Content Type

file_name.description: The name of the file. It will be auto-generated if not provided.
file_name.title: File Name

url.description: The URL where the file can be downloaded from.
url.title: Url

file_size.description: The size of the file in bytes.
file_size.title: File Size

schema.description: Whether to include logs (`1`) in the response or not (`0`).

success.description: Whether the request was cancelled successfully.
